payload.probes:
SECOND FILL. Inherits P1-P5 unchanged — nothing since has contradicted them. SEVEN ADDED (P6-P12), every one run against the real channel during the rewalk rather than reasoned about. Five of the seven came back FALSE, and four of those five were already causing damage.

== INHERITED ==

P1 — 'ripgrep will be available on the machine.' PROBE: `rg --version` on the owner's own primary machine. RESULT: FALSE — not on PATH. CONSEQUENCE: the npm package is not a convenience wrapper, it IS the delivery mechanism, and the no-fallback ruling rests on the package resolving a binary rather than on any system install.

P2 — 'git grep can search a tag ref.' PROBE: a real ref-scoped search. RESULT: PASS, in parseable ref:path:count form. The record search needs no new engine.

P3 — 'the branch/tag name collision is real.' PROBE: the same call. RESULT: CONFIRMED DEFECT — git emitted 'refname is ambiguous' and resolved to one silently. R24 is load-bearing by observation, not by argument.

P4 — 'the predecessor system is reachable as a branch.' PROBE: a ref-scoped search against its method files. RESULT: PASS — searchable with zero extra machinery.

P5 — 'applies_to is machine-readable enough to join guidance onto packets.' RESULT: FALSE, and still the most consequential finding of the milestone. Ten nodes in the whole ledger carry applies_to; ZERO machine-state nodes do; and the field's content is free prose written for a person, not a selector. R14 stands; its mechanism is an M4 decision with three candidates, and if semantic matching is a contender it needs an M5 spike, because 'does it pick the RIGHT laws' must be measured.

== ADDED BY THE REWALK ==

P6 — 'a tool built during a session can be called in that session.' This assumption sits underneath every declared workaround logged today, so it was worth settling rather than living with. PROBE: built the promotion tool, landed it on trunk, and asked the harness for it by name. RESULT: FALSE — 'No matching deferred tools found'. The tool list is snapshotted when the client connects; tools that land afterwards are invisible, however alive the engine is. SECOND HALF OF THE PROBE, run when the owner reconnected on request: the tool appeared immediately and was callable. RESULT: the constraint is the CLIENT SNAPSHOT, not the engine.
CONSEQUENCE, and it is a practical one: the declared-workaround pattern has a cheap remedy that was being treated as a law of nature. Six scripts were written today under 'the lane cannot do this yet'; at least the promotion ones could have been one reconnect instead. The RAID entry changes from 'a tool built this session cannot be called this session' to 'a tool built this session cannot be called UNTIL THE CLIENT RECONNECTS', which is a nuisance rather than a wall.

P7 — 'the boot admission survives an engine restart.' PROBE: the reconnect above. RESULT: SPLIT, and worth stating precisely because the two halves look identical from the outside. The admission now survives an ENGINE restart — that was today's fix, keying the session file to the project root instead of to a value randomised per shim start. It does NOT survive a CLIENT reconnect, and should not: a reconnect is a new session and re-attesting the contract is the point of the ritual. Cost measured: one boot round-trip. NOT A DEFECT, recorded so the next reader does not 'fix' it.

P8 — 'handing the test runner a directory runs the tests in it.' PROBE: the promotion's own suite runner, in trunk. RESULT: FALSE — the runner resolved the directory name as a MODULE and died with module-not-found. The crash was then counted as one failing test named after the directory. CONSEQUENCE: the promotion refused three times in a row, reporting a red suite, while trunk was green throughout. The refusal blamed the code for the guard's own bad argument, which is worse than no refusal — it sends the reader hunting through healthy code. Fixed by enumerating the files; R19 is the requirement it violated.

P9 — 'a test suite spawned from inside a test runs.' PROBE: called the real suite runner from a test. RESULT: FALSE — the child inherits a context variable, sees itself as nested, and DECLINES TO RUN ANY FILES while exiting successfully: zero passed, zero failed. CONSEQUENCE, and this is the sharpest finding of the rewalk: zero failures reads as GREEN. A promotion could have run nothing, reported success, and changed trunk on the strength of it. This is the direct parent of R34 — a proof that proved nothing is a failure — and it is the failure shape this iteration keeps meeting: not a wrong answer, but an absent check wearing a passing face.

P10 — 'a reopen leaves the work reachable after it is re-walked.' PROBE: the first real reopen, at this iteration's own gate_inputs. RESULT: FALSE — DEADLOCK. The gate is a three-way join; the fuel from the two arms NOT being reopened had been consumed when the gate first activated, and nothing would ever produce it again. Both reopened states were re-filled, the last edge fired, and the walk stopped: no error, no escape, no legal move, an empty active set. It looked like the machine was waiting for something. CONSEQUENCE: R31 gains its third clause, F33 is split from F34, and reopen — which had shipped with zero tests — now has four with red observed before green. Fixed and promoted.

P11 — 'dependencies can be installed before the manifest that declares them is copied.' PROBE: the first promotion attempt. RESULT: FALSE, obviously in hindsight — the install resolved against the manifest being REPLACED, so every importer of the new dependency crashed. The suite then reported the engine as broken when the truth was that a package was missing. CONSEQUENCE: ordering obligation inside F36, recorded at UC-D ext 4a precisely because someone will later look for the function that prevents it and find none.

P12 — 'two open iterations make a tool's working root ambiguous.' NOT PROBED LIVE, and I am recording that rather than implying it was. Only one iteration is open, and opening a second purely to observe a refusal would be work the owner did not ask for. The refusal itself is covered by a test with a synthetic pair of roots; what is untested is the LIVE case, where the ambiguity arises from real project state rather than from a fixture. It stays an assumption until two iterations genuinely run at once — which is the scenario the whole worktree lane exists for, so it will be settled by use rather than by a probe.

== WHAT THE PROBE SET SAYS AS A WHOLE ==
Seven probes added, five FALSE. Four of the five false ones were not predictions about the future — they were beliefs already causing damage at the moment they were tested: a promotion refusing on a phantom red, a suite that could report success without running, a reopen that stranded its own gate, an install resolving against the wrong manifest. The one probe that came back with good news (P6) made six declared workarounds partly avoidable.
That ratio is the argument for this state existing at all, and it is worth stating plainly: every one of these was cheaper to find with a probe than it was to find in use — and three of them WERE found in use first, at the cost of an hour each.
